bull.b: Double-digit revenue growth alongside higher earning assets indicates Ally is expanding its lending platform and monetizing balance-sheet growth. If maintained, broader origination volume can support recurring net interest income and provide operating scale over the next several quarters.

An 87% deposit funding mix and 3.6 million customers give Ally a substantial direct banking franchise rather than reliance solely on market funding. Continued customer growth can support scalable deposit gathering and help underpin lending growth and liquidity management.

Improving retail auto loss performance and tighter charge-off guidance indicate that credit normalization is supporting the recovery. Sustained improvement would reduce earnings volatility, strengthen risk-adjusted returns, and make planned balance-sheet growth more durable.

bear.b: Persistently elevated leverage reduces Ally’s financial flexibility if profitability or credit performance weakens. A higher debt burden can constrain capital allocation, increase sensitivity to funding conditions, and make recovery periods more difficult to manage.

Very limited and inconsistent free-cash conversion makes the reported operating cash flow less reliable as a measure of financial flexibility. Volatile free cash flow can restrict internally funded investment, distributions, and the ability to absorb unexpected balance-sheet demands.

Rapid asset growth is requiring additional expected-loss reserves, creating a recurring tension between expansion and near-term earnings. If credit costs continue rising with the portfolio, provisions could offset margin gains and make profitability more dependent on benign loss trends.
